basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Silverfort/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [Silverfort](https://silverfort.com) ITDR Admin Console connector solution allows ingestion of Silverfort events and logging into Microsoft Sentinel. Silverfort provides syslog based events and logging using Common Event Format (CEF). By forwarding your Silverfort ITDR Admin Console CEF data into Microsoft Sentinel, you can take advantage of Sentinels's search & correlation, alerting, and threat intelligence enrichment on Silverfort data. Please contact Silverfort or consult the Silverfort documentation for more information. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 20 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for Silverfort. You can get Silverfort CommonSecurityLog data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.

The [Silverfort](https://silverfort.com) ITDR Admin Console connector solution allows ingestion of Silverfort events and logging into Microsoft Sentinel.
 Silverfort provides syslog based events and logging using Common Event Format (CEF). By forwarding your Silverfort ITDR Admin Console CEF data into Microsoft Sentinel, you can take advantage of Sentinels's search & correlation, alerting, and threat intelligence enrichment on Silverfort data. 
 Please contact Silverfort or consult the Silverfort documentation for more information.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

Identifies Silverfort incidents involving abuse of Active Directory Certificate Services associated with Certifried. This behavior may allow an attacker to escalate privileges and impersonate an account in the domain.
Identifies Silverfort incidents associated with exploitation of the Log4Shell vulnerability in Log4j. Specially crafted log messages may allow an attacker to run arbitrary code on an affected system.
Identifies Silverfort incidents associated with exploitation of the NoPac vulnerabilities in Active Directory. This behavior may allow an attacker to escalate privileges and compromise the domain.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving repeated attempts to authenticate to a user account. This behavior may indicate a brute-force attempt to gain unauthorized access.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving sequential authentications between different systems. This behavior may indicate an attacker progressing through the network after compromising an account.

Identifies Silverfort incidents involving multiple failed logon attempts to the same server from different accounts within a short period. This behavior may indicate credential scanning or brute-force activity.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving bursts of authentications from one host to many other hosts. This behavior may indicate reconnaissance to identify targets for lateral movement.

elements.name: analytic8
elements.label: Silverfort - Denied MFA with risk indicators

options.text: Identifies Silverfort incidents involving denied MFA requests accompanied by additional risk indicators, such as a new host or impossible travel. This behavior may indicate a user rejecting an unauthorized authentication attempt.

Identifies Silverfort incidents involving AS-REQ messages accepted by a domain controller without pre-authentication. This behavior may indicate collection of AS-REP responses for offline password cracking.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving unusually frequent access to CIFS servers. This behavior may indicate reconnaissance of shared resources before lateral movement.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving Kerberos authentication failures caused by checksum mismatches. This behavior may indicate tampering or forged authentication packets.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving authentications from IP addresses flagged as malicious. This behavior may indicate access from attacker-controlled infrastructure.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving logons from distant locations within a short period. This behavior may indicate use of compromised credentials.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving repeated denied MFA prompts. This behavior may indicate an attacker attempting to coerce a user into approving an authentication request.

Identifies Silverfort incidents involving anomalous username inputs, such as unusually long values or special-character patterns. These inputs may indicate an attempt to inject a malicious payload during authentication.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving requests for weakly encrypted service tickets. This behavior may indicate service principal name ticket harvesting for offline password cracking.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving creation of new system services on a host. This behavior may indicate remote code execution using tools such as PsExec or PAExec.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving an account being added to a privileged group. An unexpected membership change may grant elevated access and indicate privilege escalation or persistence.

Identifies Silverfort incidents involving a security log being cleared on a domain controller. Clearing this log may remove evidence of account activity and indicate an attempt to evade investigation.
Identifies Silverfort incidents involving potential extraction of the NTDS.dit Active Directory database. Access to this database may expose domain account password hashes for credential theft.
